Class TokenizerCharacterPolicy

java.lang.Object
opennlp.tools.tokenize.TokenizerCharacterPolicy
All Implemented Interfaces:
Predicate<CharSequence>
public final class TokenizerCharacterPolicy extends Object implements Predicate<CharSequence>
An immutable policy for testing token eligibility against explicit character sets.

A token consists of one or more letters or digits. Each letter or digit may be followed by zero or more marks. A mark cannot start a token. The supplied sets express a caller's tokenization policy; this class does not infer Unicode character categories.

This predicate tests a complete candidate without finding token boundaries or changing its text.

Since:
3.0.0

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static TokenizerCharacterPolicy of(opennlp.tools.util.normalizer.CodePointSet letters, opennlp.tools.util.normalizer.CodePointSet digits, opennlp.tools.util.normalizer.CodePointSet marks)
      Creates a policy from explicit, pairwise-disjoint code point sets. Whitespace separates tokens and so cannot be part of one; every other non-surrogate code point is left to the caller.
      Parameters:
      letters - Code points treated as letters.
      digits - Code points treated as digits.
      marks - Code points permitted after a letter, a digit, or another mark.
      Returns:
      The immutable policy.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if a set is null, letters and digits are both empty, a code point occurs in more than one set, or a set contains a surrogate code point or UnicodeWhitespace member.

    • ascii

      public static TokenizerCharacterPolicy ascii()
      Returns a policy for ASCII letters and digits, with no marks.
      Returns:
      a policy for ASCII letters and digits, with no marks

    • parse

      public static TokenizerCharacterPolicy parse(String text)
      Parses the text form written by toString(): the three fields letters=, ;digits= and ;marks= in that order, each followed by zero or more comma separated hex code points (0041) or inclusive ranges (0041-005A). Hex digits may use either case; no prefix or whitespace is accepted.
      Parameters:
      text - The text form to read.
      Returns:
      The policy the text describes.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if text is null or not of that form, or if the sets it describes are rejected by of(CodePointSet, CodePointSet, CodePointSet).

    • test

      public boolean test(CharSequence input)

      Returns true if the entire input is a non-empty token accepted by this policy. Malformed UTF-16 input (an unpaired or reversed surrogate) returns false.

      Specified by:
      test in interface Predicate<CharSequence>
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - Thrown if input is null.

    • toString

      public String toString()

      Writes the text form read by parse(String), for example letters=0041-005A,0061-007A;digits=0030-0039;marks= for ascii(): runs of adjacent code points become ranges, and each code point is written with at least four upper-case hex digits.
